videos.title: Unattended stove to flashover
videos.caption:
A pan of cooking oil left on the stove. Watch how fast it spreads to the cabinets and flashes the whole kitchen over. 🔥

This is a NIST fire research test in a full-size kitchen compartment.

Cooking is the #1 cause of home fires. Never leave the stove unattended.

🎥 Video: NIST (National Institute of Standards and Technology), public domain

#firescience #flashover #kitchenfire #firefighter #fireservice #firesafety #stationhq

videos.title: Same room, same couch, one difference
videos.caption:
Two identical living rooms. The only difference: one couch has a fire barrier fabric under the cover.

In NIST's tests, the barrier delayed flashover from about 6 minutes to about 21 minutes. That's the difference between beating flashover and arriving after it. 🚒

🎥 Video: NIST (National Institute of Standards and Technology), public domain

#firescience #flashover #fireservice #firefighter #firebehavior #stationhq

videos.title: Untreated vs. treated fabric
videos.caption:
Same chair, same flame, two fabrics. Left: untreated cotton. Right: a back-coated fabric developed by NIST researchers.

One self-extinguishes the moment the flame is pulled. The other keeps going. 🔥

Upholstered furniture is the leading first item ignited in deadly US home fires.

🎥 Video: NIST (National Institute of Standards and Technology), public domain

#firescience #firebehavior #firefighter #fireservice #stationhq

videos.title: Grease fire from a few mm of oil
videos.caption:
Just 3 mm of canola oil in a frying pan. This is what happens when the burner keeps going. 🍳🔥

From a NIST test series on cooktop ignition prevention.

First-due companies know: kitchen calls can go from smoke to fire fast.

🎥 Video: NIST (National Institute of Standards and Technology), public domain

#greasefire #kitchenfire #firescience #firefighter #fireservice #stationhq

videos.title: Wind-driven apartment fire
videos.caption:
Wind-driven fire in a 7-story building on Governors Island, NY. 🌬️🔥

NIST and FDNY ran these experiments to study how wind pushes heat and fire through apartments, corridors and stairwells, and which tactics can control it.

If you've ever opened a door on a wind-driven fire, you know.

🎥 Video: NIST (National Institute of Standards and Technology), public domain

#winddrivenfire #highrise #firescience #fireservice #firefighter #stationhq

videos.title: Watered tree vs. dry tree
videos.caption:
Watered tree on the left. Dry tree on the right. Same ignition source. 🎄🔥

In NIST's test, the watered tree never caught. The dry one was fully involved in seconds and took the room with it.

Remind your community: water the tree every day.

🎥 Video: NIST (National Institute of Standards and Technology), public domain

#christmastreefire #holidayfiresafety #firesafety #fireservice #firefighter #stationhq

videos.title: Couch fire to flashover
videos.caption:
One small flame under a pillow on a cotton couch. That's all it takes. 🛋️🔥

In NIST's furnished-room tests, couches without a barrier fabric reached flashover in about 6 minutes.

By the time most crews are on scene, this room is already gone.

🎥 Video: NIST (National Institute of Standards and Technology), public domain

#flashover #firescience #firebehavior #firefighter #fireservice #stationhq

videos.title: Wind-driven fire, 7th floor
videos.caption:
7th floor, wind blowing straight into the fire apartment. 🌬️🔥

From the NIST and FDNY wind-driven fire experiments on Governors Island, NY, where researchers tested tactics like wind control devices to stop wind from pushing fire down the hall.

High-rise crews, what's your SOP on wind?

🎥 Video: NIST (National Institute of Standards and Technology), public domain

#winddrivenfire #highrise #fdny #firescience #fireservice #firefighter #stationhq

videos.title: From smoldering to flames
videos.caption:
Three cigarettes tucked in the crevices of a chair. It smolders, and smolders, and then it doesn't. 🚬🔥

NIST researchers filmed this chair mockup as it transitioned from smoldering to open flame.

The quiet fires are the dangerous ones.

🎥 Video: NIST (National Institute of Standards and Technology), public domain

#smoldering #firescience #firebehavior #firefighter #fireservice #stationhq

videos.title: Fire climbing a cable tray
videos.caption:
Watch fire race straight up a vertical tray of electrical cables. ⚡🔥

From NIST and U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission research on how cable fires spread.

Commercial and industrial companies: this is why vertical shafts matter.

🎥 Video: NIST and U.S. NRC, public domain

#cablefire #electricalfire #firescience #fireservice #firefighter #stationhq

videos.title: Smoke alarm vs. bacon
videos.caption:
Why do people pull the batteries out of their smoke alarms? Bacon. 🥓🔔

NIST researchers tested how often smoke alarms go off during normal cooking. Nuisance alarms are a big reason people disable them, and a disabled alarm can't warn anyone about a real fire.

Share this with your community: don't disable it, move it or get one designed to resist cooking alarms.

🎥 Video: NIST (National Institute of Standards and Technology), public domain

#smokealarm #firesafety #fireprevention #firedepartment #stationhq

videos.title: A dry tree, in seconds
videos.caption:
This Douglas fir sat indoors with no water for over 4 weeks. One small ignition source in the lower branches. 🎄🔥

NIST filmed it in a furnished room corner. Watch how fast it goes.

Water the tree. Every day.

🎥 Video: NIST (National Institute of Standards and Technology), public domain
